title: How to Choose a Contact Center Dialer for AI Voice Agents
summary: How contact center dialers work, the six main types, what changes when an AI voice agent takes the call, and what to compare before choosing one.
body_markdown:
Outbound calling used to be limited by headcount. Teams could only hold as many conversations at once as they had representatives working the phones, so dialers were designed to keep these reps as busy as possible.


With AI voice agents, headcount no longer caps call volume, at least in theory. An AI agent can take every call a dialer connects because it doesn’t need a break between calls, and can work every hour the calling rules allow. AI agents also cost considerably less per call than reps. Smaller teams using AI agents can afford to reach contacts who were too expensive to call with reps, such as old leads and smaller accounts.


Much-increased scale and lower cost dramatically change what reps do. Teams can hand the dialing and the waiting to AI agents while reserving their reps for conversations that need a person, such as a qualified buyer who wants to negotiate a purchase or a customer with a billing dispute.


The availability of AI voice agents should also change what a buyer is looking for in a dialer. Buyers measure traditional dialers by talk time per rep. When AI agents take the calls, rep time stops being the limiting factor. Results depend instead on what the dialer does before and after each call. A contact center that puts AI agents on outbound calls needs a dialer that’s purpose-built for AI agents.


The sections below explain how dialers work, how the six main types differ, and what criteria might reasonably influence a buyer’s decision. Throughout, special emphasis is placed on how AI dialers represent a significant advance in the marketplace.


## What is a contact center dialer?


A contact center dialer is software that places outbound calls from a list so no one dials by hand. Basic dialers connect each answered call to a rep or an AI agent. Full dialers also handle the work before and after each call, such as cleaning the list and scheduling the next attempt. Dialers started as voice tools. A growing number also reach contacts by SMS, WhatsApp, email, and chat, so buyers should ask which channels a dialer covers.


Outbound teams use dialers for:


- Lead qualification and follow-up
- Sales and telemarketing
- Proactive churn reduction
- Cross-sell and up-sell
- Appointment setting
- Collections and payment
- Surveys and feedback
- Fundraising


## How does a dialer work?


Dialers were designed to run campaigns, which are outbound programs that have specified goals, contacts, agents (human or AI), and calling rules. Before a campaign launches with the first call, an outbound team has to define the campaign and write the associated playbook. The playbook establishes the steps that a contact moves through and the outcomes (also called “dispositions” or “call dispositions”) that lead to each successive step.


Every outbound call in a campaign progresses through three phases.


1. Before the call, the dialer:


- Loads the list and removes duplicates
- Filters out numbers the team should not call
- Picks a caller ID, sometimes one with a local area code
- Decides how many lines to open at once


2. During the call, the dialer:


- Detects whether a person, a voicemail greeting, or a phone tree answered
- Connects live answers to a rep or an AI agent, along with what the CRM knows about the contact
- Lets an AI agent capture requests the contact makes, such as a time to call back


3. After the call, the dialer:


- Records the outcome of the call, often called a disposition
- Uses the outcome to set the next step, such as a retry in two days, a callback at a requested time, a text message, a transfer to a specialist, or removal from the list


After a round of calls has been completed, the dialer will report results for the campaign. The outbound team can then compare the costs of the campaign against the outcomes it achieved. Based on this data, the outbound team can change the playbook, such as adjusting the retry schedule or the next step after an outcome, before running it again.


## What are the main types of dialers?


Vendors usually sort and present dialers by how each type paces calls for the human reps available to take them. The newest type, the AI agent dialer, was designed for AI voice agents and does not pace calls around the rep workloads. The other five common types were built for human reps to use: preview, progressive, power, predictive, and parallel.


#### AI agent dialer


An[AI agent dialer](https://www.retellai.com/glossary/ai-dialer) connects calls to AI voice agents instead of to reps. Each connected call is assigned its own AI agent, so the dialer does not have to plan around human rep availability. The dialer’s only limits come from[the account's concurrency](https://www.retellai.com/learn/outbound-capacity-calculator) (the number of calls it can run at once) and the telephony provider's calls-per-second rate. With this kind of dialer in place, no contact will have to wait for an agent as long as the account is operating within its concurrency.


AI agents come built into an AI agent dialer, as opposed to traditional dialers which have to connect the agents through an integration. Most AI agent dialers also work across channels by default, meaning that a single campaign can call a contact and then follow up via SMS, WhatsApp, email, or chat (as opposed to traditional dialers built for voice first or exclusively).


AI agent dialers are well suited to high-volume outbound campaigns where each call in the campaign has a clear outcome, such as a booked appointment. Calls from an AI agent also need to follow applicable federal and[state regulations](https://www.retellai.com/blog/california-ab-1609-ai-customer-service-law) that govern the use of artificial voices. Buyers should also inquire about the campaign logic behind this type of dialer, because weak follow-up rules will ensure that fewer contacts are reached.


Be aware that some vendors may use the term "AI dialer" for dialers built for human reps with AI features added, so it’s worth[asking follow-up questions](https://www.retellai.com/blog/ai-dialer-buyers-guide) to determine what kind of dialer a vendor is actually discussing.


#### Preview dialer


A[preview dialer](https://www.retellai.com/glossary/preview-dialer) shows the rep the contact's record before the call. The rep reviews the record and starts the call. A preview dialer is best suited to complex, high-value calls in account-based sales and financial services, where the first few seconds of the conversation are heavily dependent on context. As a result of this configuration, reps on a preview dialer typically make fewer calls per hour.


#### Progressive dialer


A progressive dialer places the next call automatically, but only when a rep becomes free. It never dials ahead of the team, so it produces few[abandoned calls](https://www.retellai.com/glossary/call-abandonment-rate) . Reps using progressive dialers will wait through rings and voicemail greetings.


#### Power dialer


A power dialer works through a list one call at a time per rep and moves to the next number as soon as a call ends. The rep never dials manually and works at a steady pace. Power dialers are generally suitable for lead follow-up and sales outreach. Reps using these dialers will still hear voicemail greetings and unanswered rings.


#### Predictive dialer


A[predictive dialer](https://www.retellai.com/blog/what-is-predictive-dialing) uses statistics to forecast when reps will be free. To keep a live answer waiting when each rep finishes a call, it dials several numbers per rep. Large, steady campaigns such as collections and surveys are good use cases for predictive dialers, because the goal with these uses is the most talk time per rep. Predictive pacing also carries a high degree of compliance risk, since a person can answer when no rep is free.


#### Parallel dialer


A[parallel dialer](https://www.retellai.com/glossary/parallel-dialer) rings several numbers at once for one rep and connects the rep to the first person who answers. The dialer cancels the other calls. Sales development teams use parallel dialers to raise the number of live conversations per rep per hour. A second person who happens to answer will be on the receiving end of a dropped call, because that rep will be working the first call. Parallel dialing ensures a high volume of dials per number.


## What changes when an AI voice agent takes the call?


#### Human reps move to lead conversion


Many teams use an AI agent for the first touch and qualification, then transfer qualified contacts to a human rep. As a result, reps can focus their time on converting qualified contacts. Transfers become some of the most valuable outcomes in the campaign, because the qualified contacts are still on the line and primed for conversations. The AI dialer will work steadily while accommodating the hours and capacity of the reps who take the transfers.


#### Staffing stops limiting outbound volume


Predictive and parallel dialers will dial ahead to keep each rep talking instead of waiting. When an AI voice agent conducts the conversation, every connected call can have its own agent. The dialer no longer has to guess how many reps need to be available when a call initially connects.


#### Abandoned-call rules may not fit AI agents


A predictive dialer abandons calls when it dials ahead of the reps. Under the Telemarketing Sales Rule, an outbound call is abandoned when a person answers and the call is not connected to a sales representative within two seconds of the person's completed greeting ([16 CFR 310.4](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/16/310.4) ). The FCC's rule caps abandoned telemarketing calls at 3% of calls answered by a live person, measured over 30 days for a single campaign ([47 CFR 64.1200(a)(7)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-47/chapter-I/subchapter-B/part-64/subpart-L/section-64.1200) ). Teams often tune predictive dialers to stay just under that 3% cap. Whether an AI agent that takes the call counts as connecting to a sales representative is currently unsettled, so contact center teams using predictive dialers in conjunction with AI agents that are concerned about the applicability of this rule should get legal counsel's views.


#### Artificial-voice consent rules may apply


In February 2024, the FCC ruled that AI-generated voices are "artificial" voices under the Telephone Consumer Protection Act. Calls that use them need the called party's prior express consent, unless an emergency purpose or an exemption applies. Telemarketing calls that use an artificial voice to reach a wireless number or a residential line need prior express written consent ([47 CFR 64.1200(a)(2)–(3)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-47/chapter-I/subchapter-B/part-64/subpart-L/section-64.1200) ). Retell's[TCPA compliance playbook for voice AI outbound](https://www.retellai.com/blog/tcpa-compliance-playbook-voice-ai-outbound) covers consent, disclosure, and state rules in more detail. Again, none of the above constitutes legal advice.


## How do teams run outbound with AI voice agents today?


Teams that add AI voice agents to outbound typically use one of four setups. For each setup, count the systems one campaign will touch. Every added system means more upkeep for the team and spreads a contact's history across places the next agent may not see. A newer fifth setup puts the dialer and the AI agents on one platform.


#### Legacy dialer plus AI agents


Many teams keep calling operations on a legacy dialer inside a contact center platform such as Five9 or Genesys and connect an AI voice agent to the legacy dialer through an integration. Outcomes and context have to pass across the integration after every call.


#### Batch calling


Batch calling remains the simplest setup. A team uploads a list and the AI agent calls it once. A person on the team prepares and launches every later attempt as a new batch. Batch calling suits one-off lists, such as a single round of appointment reminders.


#### Custom-built infrastructure


Teams with engineers sometimes build the missing pieces themselves. The engineers write scripts for[local presence](https://www.retellai.com/glossary/local-presence-dialing) , contact filtering, number rotation, callbacks, and multi-step sequences. A custom build can fit a team's process closely, but someone on the vendor or customer team has to maintain it.


#### Several tools stitched together


Sometimes, teams will combine a CRM, an automation platform, spreadsheets, a telephony provider, and an AI voice agent to run a single outbound program. These teams have to move contacts and results between the tools through automations and manual exports, which can be a time-consuming and error-prone process. An opt-out recorded on a call, for example, may not reach the texting tool until someone updates it.


Teams on separate systems run into several common pitfalls:


- Connectors to the CRM and to spreadsheets break when either side changes.
- Each vendor's tool needs separate upkeep, such as one vendor for telephony and another for the language model.
- The contact center team and the customer experience team work in different tools, which prevents continuous iteration and improvement of the dialer and its agents.
- Campaign results sit in several systems, meaning the team cannot always see what to change before the next round of calls in a campaign.


#### Dialer and AI agents on one platform


The newest approach runs an AI dialer within an AI voice agent platform, such as Retell Dialer. Because the dialer, AI agents, contact records, and campaign analytics share a unified platform, context and call outcomes remain tied to each contact. This gives internal teams a single system to manage, eliminating the complexity of maintaining legacy infrastructure or piecing together multi-tool solutions.

## Frequently asked questions


#### What is an AI agent dialer?


An AI agent dialer connects each answered call to an AI voice agent instead of a human rep. Each connected call receives its own agent, so the dialer does not have to forecast when reps will be free. Its limits are the account's concurrency (the number of calls it can run at once) and the telephony provider's calls-per-second rate. Some vendors also say "AI dialer" for a dialer that serves human reps and adds AI features.


#### Do AI voice agents need a predictive dialer?


Usually not. A predictive dialer forecasts when human reps will be free. An AI voice agent can take each connected call, so a dialer built for AI agents expends its effort on[reaching people](https://www.retellai.com/blog/how-to-increase-outbound-call-pickup-rates) and handling follow-up instead. Calls made with an AI voice still need the consent the TCPA requires for artificial voices.


#### Should outbound calls go to AI voice agents or human reps?


AI voice agents suit calls with a clear goal and a short script, such as[appointment reminders](https://www.retellai.com/use-cases/appointment-reminder-calls) , payment follow-ups, and[first-touch lead qualification](https://www.retellai.com/use-cases/lead-qualification) . Human reps suit conversations that need judgment, such as negotiating a deal or handling a complaint. Many teams use both. An AI voice agent makes the first call and transfers qualified contacts to a rep. Under the Telephone Consumer Protection Act, AI voice calls need the called party's prior express consent, and telemarketing calls to mobile numbers and residential lines need prior express written consent.


#### What is the difference between a power dialer and a predictive dialer?


A power dialer calls one number per rep at a time and dials the next as soon as a call ends. A predictive dialer calls several numbers per rep and uses a forecast of rep availability to time them. Predictive dialing produces more talk time per hour on large campaigns. It also carries a higher risk of abandoned calls.


#### What is a hosted dialer?


A hosted dialer is a dialer the vendor runs in the cloud. The team uses it over the internet and does not buy or maintain hardware.


#### Are auto dialers legal?


Yes, within the rules for the call type and location. In the United States the Telephone Consumer Protection Act and the[Telemarketing Sales Rule](https://www.retellai.com/learn/tcpa-compliance-guide-for-outbound-ai-voice-calls-in-the-united-states) set consent, calling-hour, Do Not Call, and abandoned-call requirements, and many states add their own. This is a summary, not legal advice.


#### What is the 3% abandoned call rule?


The FCC limits abandoned telemarketing calls to 3% of calls answered by a live person, measured over a 30-day period for a single campaign. A call counts as abandoned when it is not connected to a live sales representative within two seconds of the person's completed greeting ([47 CFR 64.1200(a)(7)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-47/chapter-I/subchapter-B/part-64/subpart-L/section-64.1200) ).


#### What is local presence dialing?


Local presence dialing shows the contact a caller ID with their[own area code](https://www.retellai.com/area-codes-overview) . The business holds a number in that area code and places the call from it.


#### What is double dialing?


[Double dialing](https://www.retellai.com/blog/5-best-voicemail-practices-when-using-ai-voice-agents) places a second call to the same number right away when the first goes unanswered. Outbound teams use it to reach people who let the first call go to voicemail. Each dial can count toward state limits on call frequency.


#### What is the difference between batch calling and a dialer campaign?


Batch calling places one round of calls to an uploaded list. The team then exports the results and launches each later attempt as a new batch. A dialer campaign keeps running after the first round. It schedules retries and callbacks, routes each contact by the outcome of the last conversation, and can enroll new contacts as they arrive.


#### What is a call disposition?


A call disposition is the outcome recorded at the end of a call, such as booked, callback requested, interested but not ready, or do not call. In an outbound campaign, the disposition decides what happens to the contact next. A contact marked interested but not ready, for example, might move to a nurture step.


#### How much does a contact center dialer cost?


[Hosted dialers for human reps](https://www.retellai.com/blog/best-outbound-dialer-tested-and-ranked) are usually sold as a monthly or annual subscription. AI voice agent platforms usually charge by usage. Retell's voice agent pricing is[discussed here](https://www.retellai.com/pricing) .
